articles.standfirst: El meta rumano, fijo en LaLiga, tampoco rotó en Chipre en el choque de Europa League
articles.summary: El meta, fijo en LaLiga, tampoco rotó en Chipre
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez mantiene una política de rotaciones, en el caso del arranque de esta temporada múltiple por lo apretado del calendario, que en el caso de la portería no existe. Radu lo juega todo. El meta rumano tampoco rotó en el estreno de Europa League ante Omonia Nicosia y resultó ser el mejor de su equipo. Es el único futbolista que ha disputado los 630 minutos de esta temporada, los seis partidos de Liga y el de competición continental. Ya la pasada temporada, Radu disputó todos los partidos de Liga y 12 de Europa League. Sumó 50 partidos oficiales en su primera temporada en el Celta con un rendimiento notable. Esta campaña va camino de repetir cifras. La pasada temporada únicamente se perdió dos partidos de Europa League por molestias físicas y los tres partidos de Copa. Fueron los cinco encuentros que disputó Iván Villar. Esta temporada, Claudio Giráldez pidió la incorporación de un meta para elevar el nivel competitivo en la portería. Llegó Bayindir, procedente del Manchester United, pero el meta turco no ha debutado con el equipo céltico. De hecho, Claudio Giráldez ha utilizado a 25 jugadores, todos los de su plantilla menos sus dos porteros suplentes.

articles.title: Ole Miss Staff Reportedly Doubts Lane Kiffin's LSU Is 'Sincere' with Sam Leavitt's Injury Report
articles.summary: Ole Miss is planning as if LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will be on the field Saturday in Oxford, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
Ole Miss is planning as if LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will be on the field Saturday in Oxford, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel .

The Tigers listed Leavitt as doubtful on their early injury report Wednesday. Their opponents aren't buying it.

"No one on the Ole Miss staff is convinced LSU QB Sam Leavitt's appearance as 'doubtful' on the injury report is sincere and he'll miss the game on Saturday, per sources," Thamel reported.

Leavitt started LSU's first two games, throwing for 574 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions. In the season-opening win over Clemson, he ran for 113 yards and two scores on 12 carries.

ESPN's Alex Scarborough called Leavitt's injury designation "a surprising turn of events" because the junior didn't appear to be hurt during the Louisiana Tech victory or in his postgame press availability.

Scarborough added that the SEC prohibits coaches from using the injury report for the purpose of gaining a competitive edge. A player who's doubtful is "unlikely to play due to significant concerns."

A school that violates the rule can be subject to a fine of up to $100,000.

Based on Thamel's newest report, LSU coach Lane Kiffin may draw some close scrutiny from conference officials after giving the impression Leavitt is carrying an injury serious enough to potentially sideline him Saturday.

From Ole Miss' perspective, there will be a big difference between a Leavitt-led offense and one with Landen Clark or Husan Longstreet under center.

Longstreet was a 5-star recruit coming out of high school in 2025 but has thrown 16 total passes at the college level. Clark has starting experience, albeit in the FCS. He threw for 2,321 yards, 18 touchdowns and eight interceptions with Elon in 2025.

Planning to face Leavitt and having him ruled out — if it comes to that — will be less disruptive to the Rebels' game-planning than assuming he'll be inactive and having to pivot at the last minute.

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Important not to 'pigeonhole' Everton's Braiden Graham says Michael O'Neill
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says there is no rush for Everton's Braiden Graham to find his best position.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says there is no rush for Everton's Braiden Graham to find his best position.

The former Linfield attacker started his career as a central striker, a long-standing problem position for his international side.

The 18-year-old has been an unused substitute in three fixtures for Everton this season but, despite his own club's shortage of options at number nine, boss David Moyes said this month he thinks Graham is "probably someone who would play off the sides" in the Premier League.

After including Graham in the squad for a Uefa Nations League quadruple-header that begins away to Georgia on 25 September, O'Neill feels the player will be a versatile option.

"I think the most important thing is not to try and pigeonhole him into a position," he said.

"He's adaptable and he's adaptable because he's such a good player. I think at this minute in time his best option would be to play a little bit off the side, possibly as a 10, maybe around a bigger striker if you play a front-two, which not many teams do.

"What he has shown us in training, is a real high technical level and the ability to stick the ball in the net."

Eligibility rules 'not particularly fair' - O'Neill

The four-game window to start the 2026 Nations League is Graham's second time in the senior Northern Ireland panel after he was included in the squad for June friendlies against Guinea and France.

Ready to be substituted on against the latter, the final whistle was blown before he made it on for an international debut. O'Neill felt Graham "deserved" a senior bow for how he trained through the June window.

When it comes to a future position for the forward who stands at 5ft 9in, he added it was important to remember "every player develops physically differently".

"I've watched him a lot, we've watched Braiden since he was young, I've seen him from like 14 or 15," O'Neill said.

"Every player develops physically differently. It's very difficult to play in the Premier League as a striker, look at the profile of what clubs want as their striker.

"But Braiden's a very talented player, he's a very technical player, a great finisher. He has a really good left foot, he's smart in terms of how he plays."

articles.title: No. 7 LSU surprisingly lists QB Sam Leavitt as 'doubtful' for highly anticipated clash against No. 8 Ole Miss
articles.summary: Leavitt has thrown for 574 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 4 interceptions through two starts with the Tigers.
articles.body:
No. 7 LSU's first injury report ahead of its Saturday game against No. 8 Ole Miss had a massive surprise.

Quarterback Sam Leavitt was listed as doubtful by coach Lane Kiffin. SEC injury reports do not require teams to list a reason for a player's injury, and it was not publicly known that Leavitt was injured after the Tigers' Week 2 win over Louisiana Tech.

Per multiple reports, Leavitt has been limited in practice so far this week. However, ESPN reported Thursday morning that the coaching staff at Ole Miss was skeptical of the severity of Leavitt's injury and expected him to play on Saturday.

SEC rules allow the conference to fine a school and even punish a head coach for inaccurate injury reports. Injury report shenanigans "intended to hide a student-athlete's true participation status for competitive or strategic reasons" are not allowed.

Leavitt was 25-of-38 passing for 344 yards in the 45-14 win, but threw three interceptions in the first half. Like at the end of the Tigers' Week 1 blowout over Clemson, he was replaced at the end of the game by backup QB Landen Clark.

Clark would presumably start in Leavitt's absence if the Arizona State transfer can't go on Saturday.

The first SEC game of the season for either team is the biggest game of Week 3 and has been seen as one of the biggest games of the season ever since the SEC's schedule was released. As you know by now, Kiffin left Ole Miss for LSU as the Rebels were heading to the College Football Playoff at the end of the 2025 season.

His departure was protracted as he attempted to coach the team in the postseason while also still taking the job at LSU. Ole Miss rebuffed Kiffin's efforts and promoted defensive coordinator Pete Golding to replace him for the playoff and beyond. Ole Miss won its first two playoff games with Golding in charge before losing to Miami in the semifinals.

Leavitt is in his first season with the Tigers after spending the last two seasons at Arizona State. His 2025 campaign ended after only seven games when the QB suffered a season-ending Lisfranc foot injury.

In 2024, Leavitt was one of the breakout stars of college football as he and RB Cam Skattebo led the Sun Devils to the Big 12 title and a spot in the College Football Playoff.

Leavitt completed 62% of his passes for 2,885 yards and 24 TDs in 2024 with just six interceptions. He also added 443 rushing yards and five touchdowns on the ground. His passing stats were down across the board in 2025 before his season ended prematurely, but he still had rushed for over 300 yards and five scores.

This season, Leavitt is 41-of-66 passing for 574 yards and two touchdowns with four interceptions and has rushed 23 times for 135 yards and five scores. Clark is 7-of-10 passing for 109 yards and a TD with seven carries for 42 yards and a touchdown in his limited playing time so far.

If Leavitt's injury is serious and causes him to miss significant time, it'll be the second straight season where Kiffin's team has dealt with an early-season QB injury. In 2025, Ole Miss starter Austin Simmons suffered an ankle injury in Week 2 against Kentucky. He was replaced by Trinidad Chambliss, who played so well that he kept the starting job when Simmons was healthy.

Chambliss went on to finish eighth in the Heisman voting last season and returned for another season with the Rebels after the NCAA had initially denied him an extra season of eligibility.

articles.title: Nathan Broadhead: Wrexham forward to miss Wales' Nations League games with injury

articles.body:
Wrexham forward Nathan Broadhead will miss the upcoming international camp with a thigh injury.

The 28-year-old was included in Craig Bellamy's 28-man squad for Wales' Nations League A fixtures with Portugal, Norway and the Denmark double header.

But he will now withdraw from the squad due to an issue sustained in training, meaning he will also miss Wrexham's Championship fixture with Southampton on Saturday (15:00 BST).

"Broady has strained his thigh in training, which is a shame because he was training well," said Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson.

"That's going to keep him out for the weekend but there's nothing new from that."

When asked if the injury would see Broadhead miss the upcoming Wales camp, Parkinson responded: "Yes."

The 20-cap international started Wrexham's opening three Championship matches of the season but did not feature in his side's fixtures with Millwall, Swansea City, Burnley and West Ham United.

Wales travel to face Portugal on 24 September in the first of four fixtures in this newly extended international break.

They then travel to Copenhagen to take on Denmark, before World Cup quarter-finalists Norway (1 October) and the Danes (4 October) visit Cardiff.

Can Wrexham boss Parkinson bounce back again?

Wrexham boss Parkinson confirmed Josh Windass and Ben Sheaf are both in contention to feature against the Saints at the Racecourse Ground this weekend.

Last season's top scorer Windass was withdrawn at half-time of his side's 1-1 draw with Burnley in north Wales on 8 September and was an unused substitute for the 6-0 loss to West Ham United three days later.

Sheaf is yet to feature for Wrexham this season due to an ongoing knee issue, but both the midfielder and forward Windass will be available to feature against Tonda Eckert's side.

"Josh is fine, he's had a really good week and I'm pleased with him this week," Parkinson said.

"I felt he needed a good week on the training ground and he's been firing.

"Ben's also had a good week on the training ground, which he needed also."

articles.title: What to Know About Lane Kiffin's QBs Longstreet, Landen Clark amid LSU-Ole Miss' Leavitt Injury Saga
articles.summary: Amid skepticism from Mississippi about Sam Leavitt's status, the college football world is learning about Husan Longstreet and Landen Clark if either one has to start for LSU in Saturday's marquee SEC showdown.
articles.body:
Amid skepticism from Mississippi about Sam Leavitt's status, the college football world is learning about Husan Longstreet and Landen Clark if either one has to start for LSU in Saturday's marquee SEC showdown.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported on Thursday that none of the Ole Miss coaches are convinced Leavitt's is going to miss the game despite being listed on the injury report as doubtful.

In the event Leavitt does miss the game, Longstreet and Clark would be the two candidates to start in his place. All three quarterbacks were added in the transfer portal in January after Lane Kiffin's hiring.

Longstreet has a much higher pedigree as a 5-star recruit and No. 4 overall quarterback in the 2025 class. He appeared in four games at USC as a freshman, completing 13 of 15 pass attempts for 103 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions.

Clark spent last season as the starting quarterback for FCS program Elon. He threw for 2,321 yards, ran for 614 yards and accounted for 29 touchdowns in 12 games as a true freshman.

Kiffin has given Clark more run than Longstreet in the Tigers' first two games this season. Clark appeared in both games, throwing 10 passes and running the ball seven times.

Despite completing just under 56 percent of his attempts at Elon last season, Clark showed he has the physical traits to be a high-level thrower when he is asked to dropback.

Longstreet has one completion for 33 yards in LSU's 51-10 season-opening win over Clemson.

Per Pete Nakos of On3.com, Leavitt's injury is a sore throwing shoulder that has limited him in practice. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports added Leavitt didn't throw on Wednesday.

According to ESPN's Alex Scarborough , citing the SEC availability report policy, a doubtful designation describes a player as having a "25% chance to play" and any attempt at gamesmanship is considered "misleading."

Penalties for inaccurate or late injury reports include fines ranging from $25,000 to $100,000 and potential "accountability measures" for head coaches.

There was already a tremendous amount of attention on this game because Kiffin is returning to Ole Miss for the first time since his decision to take the LSU job last November while the Rebels were in the mix for the College Football Playoff.

The situation with Leavitt and LSU's quarterbacks is only adding to the intrigue of what figures to be one of the most emotional matchups of the entire season.

LSU vs. Ole Miss kicks off from Vaught–Hemingway Stadium on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET. The home team has won each of the last six meetings in the rivalry dating back to the 2020 season.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland: I spoke to players individually about Israel games - Heimir Hallgrimsson
articles.summary: Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson says he spoke to players in his Republic of Ireland squad individually about the prospect of facing Israel, adding "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games".
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson says he spoke to players in his squad individually about the prospect of facing Israel, and "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games".

Both of the forthcoming Nations League fixtures between the sides are scheduled for neutral venues, with Israel's 'home' game to be played in Hungary on 27 September, and the reverse fixture in Serbia on 4 October.

The Football Association of Ireland confirmed its 'home' tie would be played behind closed doors, while no tickets will be made available for Irish fans for their 'away' game.

After announcing his latest squad, which will also visit Kosovo on 24 September and face Austria at home on 1 October, Hallgrimsson said he had spoken to his players individually "because we shouldn't be doing this in a group talk".

"Obviously we have different opinions, different strength of opinions," he said.

"I think it's best to say, without going into individuals, none of us feel comfortable playing in these games but once we have decided to play them, we all stick together and play as one."

Republic of Ireland to play Israel games as motion passed

Republic of Ireland v Israel to be played at neutral venue

Coleman not included in Republic of Ireland squad

At an extraordinary general meeting in July, delegates backed an FAI motion to proceed with the games amid concerns that boycotting would cause "significant and lasting harm" for the association.

However, the decision has come under increasing pressure, with a 'Stop The Game' campaign launched by Irish Sport for Palestine calling for a boycott.

The campaign has received support from former manager Brian Kerr and ex-player James McClean, and May's friendly against Qatar in Dublin was disrupted when tennis balls thrown onto the pitch .

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages. In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza. The United Nations believes the retaliation has killed more than 70,000 Palestinians.

Israel has regularly denied committing genocide or war crimes and has said its actions in Gaza have been justified as a means of self-defence.

Earlier this week, FAI director of football John Martin said the games had created a "very uncomfortable situation for everyone" and insisted players "shouldn't be in a position where they get criticised".

"We want to represent Ireland with the best games and performances that we can. That's the agreement with all of us," added Hallgrimsson.

"Obviously we don't all share the same opinion. That's just human nature."

The Nations League games mark the Republic of Ireland's first competitive action since their World Cup play-off semi-final defeat by the Czech Republic in March.

Since the penalty shootout loss in Prague, they have played four friendlies, beating Grenada and Qatar and drawing with North Macedonia and Canada.

articles.title: Santiago acogerá el decisivo España-Grecia de las Ventanas FIBA
articles.standfirst: El encuentro se disputará el 29 de noviembre en el Pabellón Multiusos Fontes do Sar
articles.summary: El encuentro se disputará el 29 de noviembre en el Pabellón Multiusos Fontes do Sar
articles.body: El decisivo partido entre España y Grecia de las Ventanas FIBA de clasificación para la Copa del Mundo del próximo año ya tiene sede: se disputará en el Pabellón Multiusos Fontes do Sar de Santiago de Compostela el 29 de noviembre. En esa misma Ventana, tres días antes, la selección masculina visitará a Montenegro en un duelo también trascendental. Será la segunda visita de la selección a Galicia en menos de dos años. En noviembre de 2024, el equipo nacional jugó en Ourense un encuentro ante Eslovaquia correspondiente a las Ventanas de clasificación para el Eurobasket de 2025. El choque ante Grecia y el previo contra Montenegro tienen una enorme importancia. Con dos victorias podría valer para clasificarse, pero el billete a Qatar está en el aire después de las últimas derrotas sufridas por la selección. España hizo una primera fase casi inmaculada acabando con un balance de 5-1 tras perder el último enfrentamiento en la visita a Georgia. Al inicio de la segunda fase, el camino se ha complicado perdiendo los dos choques de la última Ventana: 89-95 frente a Portugal y 108-106 después de una prórroga contra Grecia. Los dos tropiezos dejan a España en la segunda plaza del grupo con un balance de 5-3, el mismo que Georgia y con un triunfo menos que la líder Ucrania. A ambas selecciones les tiene ganados el average. Sin embargo, la clasificación está muy apretada. Por detrás, Portugal, Grecia y Montenegro marchan con 4-4. Para la siguiente Ventana FIBA, al estar ya todas las competiciones en marcha, el seleccionador Chus Mateo no podrá contar con jugadores de Euroliga, ni de la NBA, ni de la NCAA. Será de nuevo la clase media quien tenga que mantener al equipo nacional, que tirará de jugadores del Joventut, Unicaja, La Laguna Tenerife, Manesa, Girona... Después de esos dos encuentros, aún quedará una última Ventana en la que España tendrá que visitar a Portugal (viernes 26 de febrero) y Montenegro (lunes 1 de marzo).

articles.title: Joan García solo sufre leves molestias en la rodilla
articles.standfirst: Se ha sometido a pruebas médicas
articles.summary: Se ha sometido a pruebas médicas
articles.body: Joan García se sometió este jueves por la mañana a pruebas médicas que revelaron que sufre leves molestias en la rodilla derecha. El parte médico del club catalán no descarta ni confirma la presencia del futbolista en el Sánchez Pizjuán y apunta a que todo dependerá de su evolución. No obstante, el partido es en 48 horas y Hansi Flick nunca corre riesgos innecesarios y menos teniendo en cuenta que ahora llega un parón de tres semanas. El catalán se lesionó durante el choque de ayer contra el Racing de Santander en el Spotify Camp Nou. Joan García salió de la zona de césped natural para recoger un balón y resbaló debido a las lluvias que azotaron Cataluña. Pese a que no se cayó al suelo, el meta patinó e hizo un mal gesto. De hecho, no pudo continuar tras el descanso y Szczesny se puso bajo palos. En una primera exploración, los galenos ya descartaron una lesión importante y esta mañana se ha sometido a nuevas pruebas en la Ciudad Deportiva que han confirmado dicho diagnóstico. "El jugador del primer equipo Joan García presenta leves molestias en la rodilla derecha. La evolución de la lesión marcará su disponibilidad", se limita a apuntar el comunicado. Además, la pierna que se ha lesionado no es la misma de la que se tuvo que operar la temporada pasada. Si, finalmente, el catalán es baja, Hansi Flick deberá decidir si apuesta, de nuevo, por Szczesny en el Sánchez Pizjuán o da sus primeros minutos como culé a Livakovic. De momento, ayer fue el meta polaco el encargado de suplir a Joan García cuando se lesionó contra el Racing de Santander.

articles.title: Jurgen Klopp: New Germany coach wants to 'reclaim' flag amid elections
articles.summary: New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.
articles.body:
New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.

The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won 43.8% of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, falling just short of securing an absolute majority in the regional parliament.

The anti-immigration party also expects strong results in elections on Sunday in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

Speaking at a news conference to announce his first squad, Klopp stressed he is not a political "expert" but added: "We had an election where some people may have thought it was OK, while others were saying, 'my God, what is happening here?'

"From my perspective as a sportsman, I can say that I would very much like to reclaim the flag for myself, for all of us.

"I want it so that when someone waves it, no one thinks: 'What is wrong with you?' Instead, I want people to understand: You are happy and realise how lucky you were to be born, grow up, or move to this wonderful country."

No far-right party has controlled a German state since World War Two, when the ruling Nazi party carried out the Holocaust.

"I do not want to entrust national pride to the wrong people," said Klopp, who prefers the term "positive patriotism" to "national pride", which he fears can be misunderstood.

The former Liverpool boss added: "I can be proud to be German while also being open-minded and diverse, and kind and friendly."

Klopp also said it was more important that the country had enough doctors and caregivers but said football can "foster a sense of community, so that people can truly feel the power of sport".

Klopp named 16 uncapped players in a 44-man squad for four upcoming Nations League matches over the space of two weeks.

A group of 24 players will be available against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on 24 September and at home to Greece in Augsburg three days later.

Most of those players will then return to their clubs while the other 20 players will join the group before Germany face Serbia in Munich on 1 October and Greece in Thessaloniki on 4 October.

The first group includes Premier League trio Kai Havertz (Arsenal), Kevin Schade (Brentford) and Anton Stach (Leeds), while Jamal Musiala is selected after twice collapsing during pre-season games for Bayern Munich.

Brentford's Vitaly Janelt has received his first call-up as part of the second group, which also includes Florian Wirtz (Liverpool) and Malick Thiaw (Newcastle).

Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and defender Antonio Rudiger retired from international duty after Germany's second-round exit against Paraguay at this summer's World Cup.

That led to the departure of coach Julian Nagelsmann and the subsequent appointment of Klopp, who had been working as global head of soccer for Red Bull.

articles.title: Barcelona confirm Joan Garcia diagnosis after injury scare against Racing Club
articles.summary: Barcelona have avoided the injury outcome they feared when Joan Garcia failed to return for the second half against Racing Santander.The goalkeeper underwent...
articles.body:
Barcelona have avoided the injury outcome they feared when Joan Garcia failed to return for the second half against Racing Santander.

The goalkeeper underwent medical tests on Thursday after being replaced at the interval of Barça's 7-2 victory .

The results have ruled out a major injury, with the problem limited to mild discomfort in his right knee.

Barcelona confirmed the diagnosis in an official statement, stating, "Joan Garcia is experiencing mild discomfort in his right knee. The evolution of the injury will determine his availability."

That leaves the goalkeeper facing a short spell out rather than a lengthy absence.

Garcia's night ended after he slipped while trying to collect a ball near the advertising boards.

He felt discomfort following the incident and did not return for the second half, with Wojciech Szczesny taking his place.

The sight of Szczesny warming up during the interval immediately raised concern among the Barcelona fans. Flick was also unwilling to give a strong assessment after the game before Garcia had undergone further checks.

Those tests took place at the Ciutat Esportiva this morning and provided the answer Barcelona wanted.

There is no significant injury. Garcia will instead spend the next few days working on his recovery away from competitive action.

Barcelona can breathe easier over their goalkeeper

Joan Garcia was taken off at half-time against Racing Club. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images)

Garcia has established himself as a key player since joining Barcelona from Espanyol , and losing him for an extended period would have forced Szczesny into a more prominent role.

Instead, the club acted before the problem could become something more serious.

The discomfort Garcia felt after the slip was enough for the coaching staff to take him off, avoiding an unnecessary risk in a match Barcelona were already controlling.

His availability for the next fixture will depend on how the knee responds over the coming days, as Barcelona have not provided a specific return date.

For now, though, the important part of the update is that Garcia has avoided a major injury.

articles.title: Titans need way more from John Franklin-Myers in Week 2
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers was totally ineffective in the Week 1 loss to the Jets
articles.body:
Several new Tennessee Titans players failed to meet expectations in Sunday's Week 1 loss to the New York Jets . One of the glaring ones was defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers . The Titans need Franklin-Myers to be way better versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2 .

The Titans signed Franklin-Myers to a three-year, $63 million contract in free agency. That's a hefty deal to play next to Jeffery Simmons . Franklin-Myers was brought in for his experience in Robert Saleh's system, having played under him with the Jets.

Remember that Franklin-Myers missed a huge portion of training camp with stiffness and soreness. The former Stephen F. Austin standout did not play a single snap in the preseason. Franklin-Myers got the veteran rest treatment, but it clearly had a negative impact on his Week 1 performance.

Franklin-Myers recorded just three tackles and one quarterback pressure against the Jets. Pro Football Focus slapped him with an overall defensive grade of 52.7. His PFF pass-rushing grade was a 52.8, and run-stopping score wasn't much better (55.4). Franklin-Myers was totally ineffective.

The Eagles are dealing with an injury on the offensive line. They'll be without starting left guard Landon Dickerson , who is a Pro Bowl-caliber interior blocker. The expectation is that sophomore backup Drew Kendall will replace him. Both Simmons and Franklin-Myers need to take advantage of that matchup.

The Titans paid Franklin-Myers very handsomely to be a dominant force on the defensive line. His impact was totally muted by an underrated Jets offensive line in Week 1. Nonetheless, Coach Saleh's defensive line was very disappointing. Franklin-Myers needs to help lead the charge towards improvement.

The Titans have had way too many big-money flops lately. They certainly can't afford another. It's obviously far too early to panic. Franklin-Myers is known as a consistent defensive lineman. Hopefully Franklin-Myers will perform like his usual self soon.

articles.title: La salud mental entra en juego: AFE reúne a expertos y deportistas para abordar los riesgos psicosociales
articles.standfirst: La salud mental gana peso en el deporte: AFE reúne a expertos, instituciones y deportistas para abordar los riesgos psicosociales
articles.summary: La salud mental gana peso en el deporte: AFE reúne a expertos, instituciones y deportistas para abordar los riesgos psicosociales
articles.body: La sede de la Clínica CEMTRO de Madrid acogió este jueves una jornada impulsada por la Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE) centrada en la salud mental y los riesgos psicosociales en el deporte, un encuentro que reunió a representantes institucionales, expertos médicos, fundaciones y deportistas de élite para analizar uno de los desafíos más importantes que afronta actualmente el deporte profesional. La apertura del acto corrió a cargo de María José López, directora del Departamento de Salud de AFE, acompañada por Pilar Guillén, en representación del doctor Pedro Guillén (quien luego intervino también); Marco Bensigni, director de la Fundación Laureus España; y el presidente de AFE, David Aganzo. Asimismo, participaron figuras destacadas como Belén González, comisionada de Salud Mental del Gobierno de España, y la atleta paralímpica Desirée Vila, cuyo testimonio centró buena parte de la atención de los asistentes. El objetivo del encuentro fue poner el foco no solo en el tratamiento de los problemas de salud mental, sino también en la prevención de aquellos factores que pueden generar daño psicológico en los deportistas. Una visión compartida tanto por las instituciones presentes como por los representantes del deporte profesional, en un momento en el que la salud emocional de los atletas ha dejado de ser un asunto secundario para convertirse en una prioridad. Uno de los mensajes más contundentes de la jornada lo dejó David Aganzo, quien recordó cómo ha evolucionado la percepción de la psicología deportiva durante las últimas décadas. "Hace 23 años tuve la suerte de poder trabajar con el psicólogo deportivo Carlos Carrascosa. Antiguamente nos llamaban locos por ir al psicólogo". El presidente de AFE destacó la importancia de seguir dando visibilidad a un asunto que durante años permaneció oculto dentro de los vestuarios y aseguró que cada vez existe una mayor conciencia sobre la necesidad de acompañar a los deportistas más allá del rendimiento competitivo. Aganzo también puso el acento en el papel que juegan los distintos profesionales que rodean al deportista para ayudarle a gestionar una carrera marcada por una enorme exigencia y una duración limitada. "Vamos a ver las diferentes partes de las profesiones que nos ayudan a los deportistas a tomar esas decisiones que son importantes en la corta carrera que tenemos como deportistas". Sin embargo, el máximo responsable de AFE señaló que uno de los momentos más delicados no llega durante la competición, sino cuando esta termina. En ese sentido, alertó sobre las dificultades que encuentran muchos atletas para adaptarse a una nueva realidad una vez finalizada su trayectoria profesional. "Tenemos muchísimos problemas para dejar el deporte, ya no solamente cuando somos deportistas, sino cuando dejamos de serlo". Precisamente ese mensaje conectó con la intervención posterior de Desirée Vila. La atleta paralímpica relató cómo tuvo que reconstruir su vida después de perder una pierna tras una lesión deportiva sufrida en 2015 y explicó la importancia que tuvo el acompañamiento psicológico para superar el miedo a volver a competir. Además, advirtió de otros momentos especialmente sensibles para los deportistas, como la gestión del éxito o la retirada. La jornada sirvió así para reforzar una idea compartida por todos los participantes: la salud mental ya forma parte del alto rendimiento y requiere la misma atención que cualquier preparación física. Un reto que AFE quiere seguir abordando desde la prevención, la formación y el acompañamiento al deportista durante todas las etapas de su carrera. Tras las intervenciones institucionales de apertura, la jornada 'Salud mental y riesgos psicosociales en el fútbol profesional' organizada por AFE dio paso a dos mesas redondas diseñadas para abordar el bienestar psicológico de los deportistas desde una perspectiva multidisciplinar, reuniendo a representantes del ámbito médico, sindical, institucional y social. La primera mesa, titulada "Salud mental y deporte profesional", estuvo moderada por Lucila Pascua, presidenta de la Asociación de Jugadoras de Baloncesto (AJUB) y psicóloga. En ella participaron la presidenta de la Sociedad Española de Psiquiatría y Salud Mental, Marina Díaz Marsá; la expresidenta de la Asociación Española de Médicos de Equipos de Fútbol (AEMEF), Ana de la Torre; y un representante del sindicato mundial de futbolistas AIF. El objetivo de este panel fue analizar los principales riesgos psicológicos a los que se enfrentan los deportistas profesionales, así como los mecanismos de prevención, detección y acompañamiento necesarios para proteger su salud mental. Tras una pausa, la jornada continuó con una segunda mesa redonda bajo el título "La salud mental como responsabilidad del ecosistema deportivo, laboral y social", moderada por María José López. En este debate participaron nuevamente representantes de AIF, junto a Paula Berruezo, coordinadora técnica de Investigación y Programas de la Fundación Gasol; Ignacio Martín Pina, de la Unión de Actores y Actrices; y el psicólogo deportivo José Carrascosa Oltra. La mesa puso el foco en la necesidad de implicar a clubes, instituciones, asociaciones, sindicatos y organizaciones sociales en la creación de entornos más seguros y saludables para los deportistas. "Los primeros futbolistas con los que trabajé venían a mi casa para que los entrenadores no se enteraran. Hay que generar protocolos porque se dan casos en los que se conocen todos los aspectos físicos de un joven futbolista pero no se sabe nada de su vida", reconoce Carrascosa. La jornada concluyó con la presentación de los materiales y guías del programa AFE Salud Mental, a cargo de Juan Manuel Rodríguez y José Félix Miñambres, integrantes del equipo técnico de la iniciativa. Con ello, AFE dio un nuevo paso en su estrategia para situar el bienestar emocional como una parte esencial de la protección laboral de futbolistas y futbolistas profesionales.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel transfer news: Man Utd wonderkid attracting interest from Real Madrid, Barcelona, PSG, Bayern Munich and Premier League clubs
articles.summary: JJ Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United; the 15-year-old has requested that his registration be cancelled to become a free agent; Gabriel wanted to be involved in first-team squads; United's hierarchy will keep trying to convince Gabriel to stay while he is still registered with them
articles.body:
The 15-year-old has made it clear he wants to leave Man Utd and has asked to be deregistered immediately to become a free agent.

Gabriel and his team feel United had ample opportunities to involve him more in pre-season and in first-team squads since the season started, including in the Champions League.

United's hierarchy will keep trying to convince Gabriel to stay while he is still registered with them.

However, it is understood Gabriel has made up his mind and, as far as he's concerned, has played his last game for the club.

Gabriel turns 16 on October 6 and cannot sign a scholarship agreement until then, or a professional contract until he turns 17.

Premier League rules state that a youth registration can only be cancelled if the club, player and parent or carer agree. If they cannot reach an agreement, the Premier League can make a binding decision.

Conversations now with Gabriel's team and his family will be key, and it will be up to Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and academy director Stephen Torpey to attempt to de-escalate the situation.

But the biggest clubs around the Premier League and the rest of Europe will all be monitoring the situation with Gabriel as it evolves.

He was not included in the A-list for Champions League participation and featured for eight minutes for the first team in pre-season, and there is a feeling he has not been afforded as many opportunities as other young players around the squad.

However, those inside Carrington believe not much more could have been done to show a pathway through to the senior team for the young star.

In the last 12 months, Gabriel met former United head coach Ruben Amorim in his office as a first step towards the first team, followed by a meeting not too soon after with Sir Alex Ferguson.

Gabriel then trained with the first team last season and was part of Carrick's pre-season squad at times this summer as well, making his debut against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm last month.

However, Gabriel has started this season incredibly well. He scored a hat-trick against Sabah last week in the UEFA Youth League and has two goals and two assists in Premier League 2 so far this season.

Gabriel became the youngest winner of United's Jimmy Murphy Young Player of the Year award last season after scoring more than 20 goals for the U18s.

Carrick: We have to be careful with Gabriel situation

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick has asked for Gabriel's welfare to be protected amid the doubts over the teenager's future at the club.

Carrick told Sky Sports on Wednesday: "We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy.

"It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child, really.

"The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure and how much we jump on that."

"First of all, he's an unbelievable talent. The problem now is with the lad and probably his agents and his family - I don't know him so I'm only thinking from the outside.

"When you're watching Max Dowman at Arsenal and Rio Ngumoha getting given a chance at Liverpool and doing very well, he's probably thinking, 'I should be playing at Man Utd now as well'.

"This is the problem you're going to have with the kids of this day and age. They're so talented that they want to play straight away. When I was playing, it was unheard of at 16.

"It'll be a massive blow for Man Utd. Believe me, this kid is an unbelievable talent. They'll have every club in the world wanting him."
